record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: Let MT be the fragment of QMS extending the nominal-free metric language with operators exists<a and exists<=a by adding topological interior and closure operators induced by metric quantification, together with universal and existential modalities. For metric spaces whose induced topological spaces are connected, find an axiomatisation of MT and determine the satisfiability problem.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on modal logics of metric spaces, where axiomatisations and decidability are known for several related fragments (e.g., the logic of metric and topology, distance logics) over arbitrary metric spaces, but the connected-topology version of MT is not addressed in those works. No subsequent publication explicitly settling this axiomatisation/satisfiability question for MT over connected metric topologies was located.

status_evidence.title: Modal Logics for Metric Spaces: Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems on modal logics for metric spaces, including questions about axiomatisations over connected metric topologies.
status_evidence.claim: The question is presented in a list of open problems concerning modal logics of metric spaces.

status_evidence.title: A logic for metric and topology
status_evidence.snippet: Combines qualitative interior/closure operators with quantitative metric operators; treats arbitrary metric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related axiomatisation/decidability results exist for the unrestricted class but not specifically for the connected-topology subclass.
